passage:
Gautam,
You asked what happened after the fest, so here it is, honestly. By eleven you were slurring, tripping over chairs, and when a senior bumped into you, you squared up and shouted in his face. I've never seen you like that. Then, suddenly, you went very sleepy, slumped on the steps, and it was hard to wake you. That scared me more than the shouting.
I didn't leave you. I kept you sitting up and kept talking to you. Nisha and I got you into an auto and back to the hostel, and I slept on the floor next to your bed. I'd decided that if you stopped responding, I'd call an ambulance, no question.
You're not in trouble with me. I just want you safe. Can we talk about it over chai?
Naveen

qa.q: How did Naveen and Nisha get Gautam back to the hostel?
qa.a: They got Gautam into an auto and back to the hostel.

qa.q: What scared Naveen most that night?
qa.a: Naveen was most frightened when Gautam went very sleepy and was hard to wake.

qa.q: Which of Naveen's actions were the caring ones?
qa.a: Staying with Gautam, keeping Gautam sitting up and talking, getting Gautam home, sleeping nearby and being ready to call an ambulance.

qa.q: How might Gautam feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Gautam may feel embarrassed and shaken, but also cared for, since Naveen says Gautam is not in trouble.

grounding: A friend sees slurring, aggression and heavy sleepiness, understands the danger, and stays, gets the person home and is ready to seek help.

passage: Ira, you asked why I went so quiet at the party last week. It's because of last Diwali. My roommate Sameer drank a lot at a friend's place, and at first he was just loud and stumbling. Then he got angry at a guy over nothing and tried to shove him. I pulled him away and sat him outside. Twenty minutes later he wouldn't wake up properly. I shook his shoulder and said his name loudly. Nothing, just a groan. I didn't wait to see if he'd sleep it off. I called an ambulance and stayed with him till it came. The doctor said calling was the right thing. People laughed, and some still call me "Ambulance Harish". I don't care. Sameer's fine now. So when I see someone that drunk, yes, I go quiet. I'm watching them.

qa.q: When did this happen?
qa.a: It happened last Diwali.

qa.q: Why does Harish go quiet around very drunk people now?
qa.a: Harish feels watchful and uneasy, remembering how Sameer stopped waking up properly.

qa.q: What choice did Harish make when Sameer wouldn't wake, and why was it right?
qa.a: Harish called an ambulance instead of waiting to see if Sameer would sleep it off, and stayed with him; the doctor said calling was right.

qa.q: How might Sameer feel about Harish's so-called overreaction now?
qa.a: Sameer would likely be grateful, since the call got him help when he could not wake up.

grounding: A friend notices stumbling, aggression and then unresponsiveness, stays with the person and calls for help.

passage: I was at the next table at the college farewell dinner, so I saw most of it. Nilesh had been drinking since the start. By eleven he was slurring, knocking over glasses, and when a waiter asked him to sit, he got loud and shoved a chair. Then, suddenly, he went very sleepy, head on the table. Rajni, from his class, didn't laugh like the others. She sat right beside him and kept saying his name. When he didn't answer properly, she turned him on his side on the bench and told me to call an ambulance. I did. She stayed with him the whole time, holding his wallet and phone, and rang his roommate. I don't know what she was feeling. Her hands were shaking, but her voice was steady. The paramedics said she'd done the right thing.

qa.q: What did Rajni ask the narrator to do?
qa.a: Call an ambulance.

qa.q: What does the narrator think Rajni might have been feeling?
qa.a: The narrator is not sure, but her shaking hands and steady voice suggest she was frightened yet determined.

qa.q: Why were Rajni's actions caring and wise?
qa.a: She stayed with Nilesh, kept him on his side, got medical help when he would not respond properly and contacted his roommate.

qa.q: How might Nilesh feel when he learns what happened?
qa.a: He may feel embarrassed and shaken, but grateful that Rajni stayed with him.

grounding: Shows, through an onlooker, a friend seeing someone slurring, aggressive and then very sleepy, staying with him and getting medical help when he is unresponsive.

passage:
Friday: At the college fest, Uday saw Farida near the stage, slurring and swaying. When a stranger bumped her, she shouted and shoved him. Then she almost fell asleep standing up. Uday felt his stomach drop. He stayed right beside her, got her water, and called her roommate Tanya. Together they took an auto back to the hostel and told the warden, who checked on her through the night.
Saturday: Farida texted, 'Sorry. I don't remember much. Thank you for not leaving.'
Monday: Over chai, Uday said, 'You scared me. I'm not judging you. I just want you safe.' Farida went quiet, then said she'd been drinking a lot since her parents' divorce. Uday suggested the college counsellor, and she agreed to go.

qa.q: Who did Uday call for help at the fest?
qa.a: Farida's roommate Tanya.

qa.q: What was Uday feeling when he saw Farida swaying?
qa.a: He was frightened and worried, feeling his stomach drop.

qa.q: What did Uday do that kept Farida safe?
qa.a: He stayed with her, gave her water, called her roommate, took her home and told the warden.

qa.q: How might Farida have felt reading back her own text on Saturday?
qa.a: She was probably embarrassed and grateful that Uday did not leave her.

grounding: Shows a friend seeing someone slurring, aggressive and very sleepy, recognising she may be unsafe, staying with her and getting her home safely.

subtopic: Caffeine, nicotine, alcohol and other substances
passage: Farida, you're going to college parties now, so let your Naveen Mama tell you one story. When I was twenty, at a friend's birthday in Hyderabad, my friend Sunil drank far too much. At first he was loud, then he started picking fights. Then, near midnight, he slumped down in the corner and wouldn't wake up properly. Everyone laughed and said let him sleep it off. I didn't like the look of him. His breathing was strange. So I stayed. I turned him on his side, the way our first-aid teacher had shown us, and told my friend to call an ambulance. The doctors said later it was a good thing we did. Sunil and I are still friends. So promise me: if a friend can't be woken, don't laugh, don't leave. Stay and get help.

qa.q: Where was the birthday party?
qa.a: In Hyderabad.

qa.q: What did young Naveen feel when he saw Sunil slumped in the corner?
qa.a: He felt uneasy and worried, not liking the look of him or his strange breathing.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Naveen's story?
qa.a: Choosing to stay with Sunil, turning him on his side and getting an ambulance instead of laughing with the others.

qa.q: How might the friends who laughed have felt later?
qa.a: They were probably shocked and ashamed when they realised how serious it had been.

grounding: Shows, through an elder's memory, a friend recognising that someone slurring, aggressive and unresponsive is unsafe, staying with him and getting medical help.

passage: The rain started just as the party thinned out, and Aadhya's phone was on four percent. Across the room Aditi was laughing at nothing, slurring her words, then leaning on the wall with her eyes half closed. When Aadhya touched her arm, Aditi mumbled, "Just leave me, I'll sleep here." A guy nearby said, "She's fine, let her crash." Aadhya didn't think so. She sat Aditi on the sofa, kept talking to her, and borrowed the host's phone to call Aditi's flatmate, who came with a cab. Aadhya rode with them, holding Aditi's hand, checking she still answered to her name. At the flat Aditi opened her eyes and sipped water. "If she stops answering, we call an ambulance straight away," Aadhya told the flatmate, and stayed the night on the floor beside the bed.

qa.q: Whose phone did Aadhya borrow to call for help?
qa.a: She borrowed the host's phone.

qa.q: What was Aadhya feeling when the guy said to let Aditi crash, and how can you tell?
qa.a: She was worried and uneasy; she didn't believe him and stayed close, talking to Aditi and calling for help.

qa.q: Which of Aadhya's actions kept Aditi safe?
qa.a: Staying with her, calling the flatmate to get her home, checking she answered to her name, and planning to call an ambulance if she stopped responding.

qa.q: What would have happened to Aditi if everyone had taken the guy's advice?
qa.a: Aditi might have been left alone and unsafe, with nobody noticing if she stopped answering.

grounding: Shows a friend who sees someone slurring and very sleepy recognising she may be unsafe, staying with her, getting her home and being ready to seek help.
